merger_description:
Amazon.com, Inc. (**Amazon**) proposes to acquire Globalstar, Inc (**Globalstar**), its subsidiaries, assets and facilities.

Amazon supplies retail services, media content, electronic devices and on-demand technology services (including cloud computing). Amazon also operates Amazon Leo, which will supply high-capacity broadband/fixed satellite service (**FSS**) services to government agencies, business and consumers using low Earth orbit satellites. Amazon Leo plans to launch its commercial service in mid-2026. In Australia, Amazon Leo has an agreement with NBN Co to deliver fixed-satellite broadband services to regional, remote and rural Australian customers.

Globalstar supplies global narrowband/mobile satellite service (**MSS**) connectivity services for voice and data communications applications. Globalstar provides these services to government agencies, businesses and consumers, using allocated MSS spectrum.

Globalstar currently provides Apple with direct-to-device (**D2D**) satellite connectivity services on certain iPhone and Apple Watch models, allowing users to send and receive messages while outside of cellular and Wi-Fi coverage (e.g. to text emergency services or receive roadside assistance). Amazon has signed an agreement to continue providing Apple with D2D services post-acquisition.

determination_table_content.details:
When making a determination in Phase 1, the Australian Competition
and Consumer Commission (ACCC) undertakes a competition
assessment and considers whether it is appropriate for an
acquisition to be approved or subject to further assessment in
Phase 2 in accordance with section 51ABZJ of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act). In doing so, the ACCC must have
regard to the object of the Act and all relevant matters, including the
interests of consumers.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notified acquisitions, see the ACCC’s merger assessment guidelines
and interim merger process guidelines.
In conducting its competition assessment, the ACCC has considered
the information and documents that were submitted with the
notification form and information from third parties.
The ACCC has determined that the Acquisition may be put into
effect as it considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to have the
effect of substantially lessening competition in any market. In
reaching its decision, and based on the material before it, the ACCC
makes the following findings.
• The Parties do not compete closely in the supply of satellite
services in Australia, as they hold spectrum authorisations in
different frequency bands and their offerings serve different use
cases.
• Post-Acquisition, the merged entity would continue to face
competition from several alternative suppliers of FSS and MSS
services, including other entities (such as SpaceX’s Starlink)
which supply both services.
